items.basis: The claimed mechanism of spacer-induced turbulence and electrostatic repulsion fails to account for the complex, dynamic nature of SMP and EPS layers which form cohesive biofilms that are not merely disrupted by shear stress but actively reorganize and adapt to flow conditions, as demonstrated in [doi:10.1016/j.memsci.2007.06.026] which shows spacers only provide temporary relief before fouling patterns adapt.

The candidate completely ignores the critical boundary condition of varying wastewater composition across municipal systems, with different pH, ionic strength, and organic content that would drastically alter the electrostatic repulsion effectiveness, contradicting [doi:10.30684/etj.30.19.14] which documents significant performance variations across different municipal wastewater sources.

The candidate's evidence bundle lacks any direct evidence supporting the combined mechanism, with [doi:10.1016/j.desal.2009.09.140] actually showing that air sparging (a different turbulence mechanism) provides better fouling control than spacers alone, and [doi:10.3390/membranes13030300] demonstrating that high-rate systems actually increase SMP production.

The candidate fails to establish any quantitative improvement over baseline, with [doi:10.1007/s11356-026-38139-3] showing that even advanced modifications like ZnO nanoparticles only provide marginal 15-20% permeability improvements, suggesting the proposed mechanism would likely be lost in the noise of real-world operational variations.

The coating of hollow fibers with charged polymers is practically impossible to implement at scale due to the microscopic surface area of thousands of fibers in a module, with no evidence in the bundle addressing the manufacturing challenges or durability of such coatings in the harsh chemical environment of wastewater treatment.
